```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from _helpers import fig, table, single, flat_table, read_flat, gallery
```

Principal coordinates analysis (PCoA) of genomes on three feature matrices: codon frequencies, amino-acid frequencies and gene-structure statistics. PCoA uses one genome per genus (best BUSCO, then N50, then lowest id), taken from genomes with complete codon, amino-acid and gene-structure data. Genera with no such genome are left out; the counts are in the table below.

Gene-structure statistics are standardized and then z-scores are clipped at ±4, so a few extreme genomes do not dominate the axes. `n_clipped_values` and `n_genera_clipped` in the tables give the number of values and genera changed.

PERMANOVA uses 999 permutations, by phylum and by order. `R2_adj` is the adjusted R² = 1 - (1 - R²)(n - 1)/(n - k) for n genera and k groups. The by-order R² is inflated by the number of groups (about 190), so use `R2_adj` when you compare by-phylum and by-order results. When a grouping has too few genera or groups, the table says it was not tested. The permanova tables report negative eigenvalues: `n_negative_eigen` is their number, `neg_eigen_over_abs_total` is their summed size divided by the summed absolute size of all eigenvalues, and `neg_eigen_over_pos_total` is their summed size divided by the summed positive eigenvalues. `n_permutations_run` is the number of permutations actually run. Read the variance shown on the axes with the negative eigenvalues in mind.

## Genera used

```{python}
flat_table("ordination_summary", "ordination")
```

## Codon frequencies

```{python}
single("O01_codon_pcoa_phylum", "PCoA of codon frequencies, coloured by phylum.", "ordination", "75%")
single("O02_codon_pcoa_class", "PCoA of codon frequencies, coloured by class.", "ordination", "75%")
flat_table("codon_permanova", "ordination", columns=["grouping", "metric", "n_genera", "n_groups", "pseudo_F", "R2", "R2_adj", "p_value", "n_permutations_run", "n_negative_eigen", "neg_eigen_over_abs_total", "neg_eigen_over_pos_total", "caveat"])
```
